bull.t: Seralutinib shows multidimensional clinical and mechanistic support
bull.b: The clinical benefit, supportive secondary endpoints and imaging evidence provide a broader efficacy thesis than a single measure. These signals may strengthen differentiation and regulatory discussions, although the primary endpoint’s statistical miss remains a constraint.

bull.t: Defined FDA pathway supports potential seralutinib submission
bull.b: A scheduled regulatory interaction and defined submission timeline give the lead program a concrete development path. If FDA feedback remains supportive, this can convert late-stage clinical assets into a potential commercial opportunity.

bull.t: Milestone-linked financing could extend development runway
bull.b: Committed and milestone-based financing can fund regulatory execution and late-stage development while reducing immediate dependence on repeated capital raises. Investor participation also provides external support for the seralutinib strategy.

bear.t: Heavy cash burn and persistent unprofitability
bear.b: Large operating losses and sustained cash outflows indicate that the business is not yet self-funding. Continued development and commercialization spending will require financing or major revenue growth, increasing execution and dilution risk.

bear.t: Negative equity and shrinking asset cushion
bear.b: Negative equity and a materially smaller asset base reduce financial flexibility and the cushion available to absorb further losses. This weak balance sheet leaves the company more exposed to financing conditions and operational setbacks.

bear.t: Primary endpoint miss increases regulatory uncertainty
bear.b: Missing the study’s prespecified statistical threshold weakens the evidentiary foundation for approval and may require FDA reliance on secondary or confirmatory data. This creates lasting uncertainty around filing acceptance, review and approval timing.
